items.picture: Emma and Lucia at a viewpoint above Bratislava: the Old Town's red roofs and church spires, the castle on its hill, the Danube curving past.
A small village in a green valley: a handful of houses with red roofs, a little church, hens in a yard. Emma and Lucia walk up the road with backpacks.
A sunny square in the Old Town: a fountain in the middle, café tables, old pastel-coloured houses. Emma crosses it with a takeaway coffee.
On a narrow Old Town street, Emma stops and tips her head back to look up at an old church with a very tall spire.

items.text: Hrad je starý. = The castle is old.
items.picture: Bratislava Castle, a big white castle with four corner towers, on its hill above the Old Town. Emma and Tomáš climb the cobbled path up to it.
The long modern bridge over the Danube with one tall pylon and a round saucer on top. Tomáš cycles across it.
Emma and Lucia sit at a café table on the Danube embankment, chatting over coffee; behind them the wide river flows under a long bridge.
A slender tower block soars high above the low houses around it. Emma and Lucia, tiny at its foot, crane their necks to see the top.

items.text: Kostol je vysoký. Lucia says this. What is tall?
Prepáčte, kde je pošta? = Excuse me, where's the post office?
items.picture: On a busy street, Emma, a postcard in her hand, politely stops the woman with the shopping bag to ask the way.
The café near the university: small round tables, a big street window, a counter with a coffee machine. Emma and Lucia sit by the window with coffee and cake.

items.text: Emma wants a coffee. Where does she go?

items.picture: In a dark cinema, Emma, Lucia and Tomáš sit in a row sharing popcorn, their faces lit by the screen; Lucia gasps.
Evening outside a grand old theatre with columns, its windows glowing. Emma and Lucia, dressed up, climb the front steps.
In a quiet museum hall full of old folk costumes and painted pottery in glass cases, Emma leans in to look while Tomáš stifles a yawn.

items.text: doľava – doprava = (to the) left – (to the) right
items.picture: At the dormitory door, pán Kováč explains the way, pointing left with one hand and right with the other; Emma, a city map in her hands, tries to follow.

items.text: Choďte rovno, potom doprava. = Go straight on, then right.
items.picture: The woman with the shopping bag points straight down the street, then sweeps her hand to the right; Emma nods along.

items.text: Choďte doľava. What does pán Kováč tell Emma?
Pošta je oproti. = The post office is opposite.
items.picture: Emma stands on the pavement with her postcard; right across the street is the post office, a yellow postbox by its door. She smiles: found it.

items.text: Čo robíš? — Som kuchár. = What do you do? — I'm a cook.
items.picture: In the kitchen of Marek's restaurant, Marek in his chef's jacket stirs a big steaming pot and grins at Emma, who peeks in through the kitchen door.
In Marek's restaurant, Dušan the waiter carries three plates at once between the tables.
In the clothes shop, a young salesman holds up two boxes to show Emma, smiling and ready to help.
Outside the university, a young journalist, a man with a notebook and a microphone, interviews pani Horváthová, who looks pleased and a little flustered.
A bus driver in a uniform cap sits at the wheel of a city bus and waves Emma aboard through the open door.
The pensioner feeds pigeons from a park bench, his walking stick resting beside him.
Two halves. Left: a young man with a backpack skateboards past. Right: the pensioner walks slowly with his stick.

In the dorm room, Emma sits on her bed beside Lucia and shows her a family photo from home in Ireland: Emma's mum, Emma's dad, Emma's brother and sister and Emma herself, all smiling in their living room.

items.text: mama a otec = mum and dad
items.picture: At home in Ireland, Emma's mum sits on the living-room sofa next to Emma's dad, his arm round her shoulders, the two of them smiling as if for a photo.

items.text: brat a sestra = brother and sister
items.picture: Marek and his younger sister Lucia goof around in the dorm kitchen: he ruffles her hair and she elbows him, both laughing.

items.text: syn a dcéra = son and daughter
items.picture: In the small back garden at home in Ireland, Emma's dad stands with an arm round each of his two younger children, his son and his daughter: Emma's brother and sister. All three grin.

items.text: manžel a manželka = husband and wife
items.picture: On a Sunday afternoon, pani Horváthová and her husband, pán Horváth, stroll arm in arm across the Old Town square; Emma, passing with a coffee, waves to them.

items.text: ženatý / vydatá = married (of a man / of a woman)
items.picture: Pán Horváth and pani Horváthová sit side by side on a park bench and hold up their hands to show their gold wedding rings, smiling.
Two halves for the two meanings. Left: at the supermarket checkout, Emma looks at her full trolley and asks how much it all costs. Right: Lucia just stands at a tram stop, waiting.
